p.title: Grok Bot Daily Lesson
p.summary: Monday, November 9, 2026 · Good morning, Shea. This week: Pages — put meal plans, dashboards, and explainers somewhere you can reopen, instead of burying them in chat.

p.heading: This week's lesson: Pages, a home for work you come back to

c: Skills decide how a Bot works. Routines decide when. Pages decide where the finished result lives. A page is a report, memo, dashboard, tracker, or explainer your Bot builds in chat: text, tables, charts, and filters you can reopen from the Library or a link.

Official help is clear on a few points that matter at home. Ask for a page in chat and the Bot posts a card. Filters and switches on the page only change what you see; they do not save edits. To change the page itself, ask the Bot. A new page starts private; you share it with the share control (team, invitees, or anyone with the link). Public links open on pages.grok.bot with no sign-in, so keep private family details off those.

steps.title: Say what the page is for
steps.detail: Name the job and what should be on it. Example: a keto week dinner board with nights, sides for the kids, and a grocery checklist.

steps.title: Open the card, keep chatting beside it
steps.detail: On desktop the page fills the window and chat stays in a side panel. On iPhone, tap the card. Ask for tweaks while you look at it.

steps.title: Tell the Bot what to change
steps.detail: Controls on the page are view-only. Say things like "Move pizza to Monday and push chicken to Tuesday" so it edits the same page.

steps.title: Pin or share only when it helps
steps.detail: Pin meal plans and the usage dashboard in the Library. Share a public dinner recipe page to Discord if you want; keep health trackers private.

steps.title: Reuse the same page next run
steps.detail: For weekly work (meal plan, usage report, this lesson), ask the Bot to refresh the existing page so the link stays the same.

c: "Refresh our keto meal plan Page for this week. Keep the same Page and link. Layout: one row per night Mon–Sat with the main dish, a note for kids' sides, and a short grocery list under it. No health numbers. When it's ready, give me only the link and one line on what changed."

When something should go to Nicole, put the shareable facts on a page (or a short email draft for Giles) instead of pasting a long chat dump. Her Bot Giles can open a link; you still approve any send.

A new routine does not run the moment you save it. If you set "every day at 8 AM" at 8:05, the first run is tomorrow at 8. Open the routine and hit Test to try it now — and use a safe example, because a test does real work. Keep anything that messages Nicole, posts to Discord, or spends money behind your OK.

p.heading: Use case spotlight: Messages connector on desktop

c: Grok Bot now has a Messages connector on desktop!

Handy for family texts you already handle by hand. Pair it with the same approval habit you use for Giles email: draft first, you tap send. On iPhone you already lean on calendar and reminders; desktop Messages is another channel to wire carefully, not a firehose.
Pick one recurring result that still lands as a long chat reply and move it onto a Page:

p.lead: Page instead of a wall of text

c: "From now on, when you finish the weekly keto meal plan, update the existing Meal Plan Page in place and reply with only the link plus a two-line summary. Same for the Weekly Usage Dashboard on Mondays. Don't paste the full body into Discord or chat."
If you already do this for dinners and usage, try it next for a one-page "week at a glance" from your iPhone calendar before the morning rundown.

rows.detail: Say "take a look at my screen" and it screenshots what you see — handy for calendar or Discord layout questions.

rows.detail: BotPlainly walks through compare-and-buy cards, and why leaving a card out of Vault keeps every payment behind your OK.

rows.detail: Show a browser flow once, review the draft skill, test on a safe example, then put it on a routine.
